newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope accepts resignation of Scottish bishop.
newsitem.headline: Pope accepts resignation of Scottish bishop.

text.p: Pope John Paul has accepted the resignation of Bishop Roderick Wright, the Scottish Roman Catholic prelate reported by media to have run off with a divorced woman, the Vatican said on Thursday.
Wright, the 55-year-old bishop of Argyll and the Isles, had turned in his resignation to the Pope last Monday.
Wright sparked a furore in Church circles when he disappeared on September 9 at the same time as divorced mother Kathleen Macphee also went missing from her Highlands home.
The Vatican made no mention of the details of the case but said the resignation had been accepted according to the norms of part two of Church canon (law) 401, which says:
"A diocesan bishop who, because of illness or some other grave reason, has become unsuited for the fulfilment of his office, is earnestly requested to offer his resignation from office."
In a statement released last Monday by the Catholic Church in Scotland, Wright said he was "physically and spiritually" unable to sustain the responsibilities of his office.
